_why: The smoke set is small, so one wrong answer moves accuracy by several points and ECE by more. These are the bars for a set this size: the real regression set (file 28) carries its own, tighter ones. A gate nobody can pass is a gate somebody deletes.

forecast._why: Four of the eighteen cases are ones the engine is designed to get wrong: it cannot see through a gauge blackout, it cannot know an unsurveyed division's hazard zone, and it has no elevation or waterway input so a riverside division can flood without any slope signal. Those cases are in the set on purpose - without them the low-confidence bins are empty and the calibration number means nothing. So the accuracy bar sits below them and ECE is the real gate, at the 0.15 build file 13 requires.

warning._why: The opposite shape to the forecast agent's, and for the opposite reason. Template selection is a lookup over a published catalogue, so it is right by construction whenever the catalogue has the template - there is no case here the rules are designed to miss, and with fifteen cases 0.95 means every one of them. Accuracy is the gate. ECE is reported and sits near 0.10 because the agent states 0.90 and is right rather more often than that; that is systematic under-confidence over a rule table, which is the honest shape, and manufacturing a spread of confidences to flatten it would produce a number that looks like a calibrated safety property and is not one.

intake._why: This eval scores the DEGRADED path - keyword matching over the trilingual lexicon with no model provider - because a fixture whose answer depends on a provider being reachable is one that fails in CI on a bad afternoon. Accuracy is the gate, at 0.85: the set deliberately contains reports a keyword list cannot resolve (a flooded road to a hospital is both an infrastructure failure and a flood), and removing them would report the degraded path as though it were the real one.
intake._why_ece_is_loose: ECE here is ~0.53 and that is correct rather than a defect. The degraded path states a FIXED confidence of 0.45, chosen to sit below the 0.70 review threshold so that every keyword extraction is confirmed by a person. It is a policy constant, not a belief, so it does not track how often the path happens to be right - and on this set it is right 93% of the time, which is where the calibration error comes from. The only way to 'fix' it would be to raise the constant above the review threshold, which would start auto-publishing keyword guesses into life-safety decisions. So the bar is set where it does not force that, and ECE is reported rather than relied on. When a model provider is configured the extraction confidence is the model's own and calibrating it becomes meaningful; that is the number worth gating on, and it needs a fixture set this repository does not have yet (file 28).

triage._why: Each case is a whole queue and the label is whether rank correlation with the dispatcher's ordering clears the 0.85 target from the proposal. Build file 16 is explicit that agreement must be measured as rank correlation on the same incident set rather than as binary agree/disagree - a dispatcher who works the queue in a slightly different order has not disagreed with it, and scoring that as a failure would push the formula towards whichever ordering happened to be in the fixtures.
triage._why_ece_is_tight: ECE sits near 0.01 because the stated confidence IS the measured agreement - the formula is deterministic and has no separate belief about its own ordering, so inventing one to fill the field would have been the dishonest option. The number is therefore self-calibrating by construction and is not evidence of anything; accuracy is the gate.
triage._the_honest_caveat: The dispatcher orderings in these fixtures are AGREED EXPECTATIONS, not recorded shifts. No labelled corpus of real dispatcher decisions exists yet, so this is a regression gate on the weighted formula rather than a measure of agreement with a human. The proposal's >=85% agreement target is validated during the pilot, and until then this number must not be quoted as though it had been.
